app.title: TraceChain - A supply-chain traceability blockchain simulation
app.subtitle: Follow a batch of coffee from the growing region to the consumer
app.simulationNotice: This is a simulated blockchain environment for learning. It is not connected to any real blockchain network.
app.permissionedNotice: The model simulated here is a permissioned blockchain: only recognized organizations can write transactions.
start.heading: Start the activity
start.objectivesHeading: After this activity you will be able to
start.objective1: Explain how a physical batch is represented as a digital asset on the ledger
start.objective3: Distinguish current state from transaction history
start.objective4: Explain why a committed record is corrected rather than deleted
start.objective5: Determine recall scope from provenance relationships
start.objective6: State the limits of blockchain regarding the truthfulness of input data
start.restartConfirmBody: All progress and scores from your previous session will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
status.standalone: Standalone mode: progress is being saved in this browser and has not been sent to Moodle.
stage.orientation.title: Step 1 - Meet the simulated blockchain network
stage.orientation.instruction: Before writing anything to the ledger, look at the real supply chain and the organizations in it. The coffee batch is a physical object; the ledger record is only a digital representation of it.
stage.orientation.supplyChainAlt: Supply chain diagram: producer co-operative, certification body, logistics provider, processing plant, distributor, retailer, consumer and regulator.
stage.orientation.checkQuestion: Does blockchain automatically prove that the original data is true?
stage.orientation.checkOptionYes: Yes. Once data is on a blockchain it is certainly true.
stage.orientation.checkOptionNo: No. Blockchain helps establish who wrote the data and whether it has changed, but it does not prove the data is true.
stage.orientation.checkOptionPartly: Yes, if the transaction is endorsed by several organizations.
stage.orientation.checkFeedback: Blockchain can help establish who recorded data, when it was recorded, and whether it has been altered; but the truthfulness of the input still has to be verified by procedures, inspections, and the accountability of the participating organizations.
stage.orientation.noPenaltyNotice: This question is not scored. It is here so you can check your own starting assumptions.
stage.createBatch.title: Step 2 - Create the coffee batch on the ledger
stage.createBatch.instruction: You are the production manager at the co-operative. Create the first record for the green coffee batch just harvested. This will be the first transaction, and it will be written into the first block of the ledger.
stage.createBatch.action.create: Create the record for the 100 kg green coffee batch and write the transaction into the first block.
stage.createBatch.sealBlock: Write the transaction into a block
stage.createBatch.sealBlockHelp: In a real blockchain a block may contain many transactions. Here we write it immediately so you can watch the first block form.
stage.anchorCertificate.title: Step 3 - Anchor the quality certificate
stage.shipAndMonitor.title: Step 4 - Hand over and monitor transport
stage.receiveAndCorrect.title: Step 5 - Receive the batch and correct the error
stage.transformBatch.title: Step 6 - Transform green coffee into roasted coffee
stage.packageAndDistribute.title: Step 7 - Package and distribute the finished product
stage.verifyAndTamper.title: Step 8 - Verify provenance and attempt tampering
stage.recallAndDebrief.title: Step 9 - Trace and recall the product
stage.notYetAvailable.heading: This step arrives in the next update
stage.notYetAvailable.body: You have completed the steps available so far. Your progress has been saved and will be restored when you return.
stage.anchorCertificate.instruction: You are the certification officer. Decide how the quality certificate should be recorded on the ledger, then examine a certificate issued by an organization that is not recognized.
stage.shipAndMonitor.instruction: The co-operative hands the batch to the carrier. Decide what this transaction actually transfers, then record the transport conditions the sensor reports.
stage.receiveAndCorrect.instruction: The plant receives the batch and reweighs it. The actual quantity does not match the dispatch manifest already on the ledger. The old record cannot be edited or deleted, so you must add a correction transaction.
stage.receiveAndCorrect.action.receive: Receive the batch from the carrier and record the purchase of ownership.
stage.receiveAndCorrect.action.correct: Submit a correction for the weight actually received; the original record is not edited.
stage.transformBatch.instruction: Roast 100 kg of green coffee into 82 kg of roasted coffee. The input batch is marked as consumed, and a provenance relationship is created between the two.
stage.transformBatch.action.transform: Roast 100 kg of green coffee into 82 kg of roasted coffee and record the provenance link.
stage.packageAndDistribute.instruction: Package 82 kg of roasted coffee into 820 packages of 100 g, transfer ownership to the distributor while the goods remain at the plant, then ship to the retailer.
stage.packageAndDistribute.action.packag: Package 82 kg of roasted coffee into 820 units of 100 g.
stage.packageAndDistribute.action.dispat: Transfer ownership to the distributor, then dispatch the goods to the retailer.
stage.verifyAndTamper.instruction: View the public information a consumer sees when scanning the QR code, then try altering an old record on a copy of the ledger and observe what happens.
stage.verifyAndTamper.publicHeading: Public information shown when the QR code is scanned
stage.verifyAndTamper.publicNotice: This is what a consumer sees. Wholesale prices and internal data do not appear here, although they remain on the ledger where only authorised parties can read them.
stage.verifyAndTamper.tamperHeading: Try altering a record that has already been committed
stage.verifyAndTamper.tamperIntro: The simulation copies the ledger, then alters the quantity on one transaction in the copy. Your real ledger is not affected.
stage.verifyAndTamper.step1Detail: Transaction {transaction} was changed from {original} to {tampered}. The record no longer matches its own hash, so the system detects it immediately.
stage.verifyAndTamper.step2Detail: If the forger recomputes the hash to match, the transaction stops being flagged. But the block containing it committed to the old hash, so block {block} no longer matches.
stage.verifyAndTamper.step3Detail: Repairing the block hash in turn breaks every block after it, because they recorded the old hash. Blocks broken: {count}.
stage.verifyAndTamper.conclusion: None of the steps above was prevented. A blockchain does not stop data being altered; it makes altering it impossible to hide. Repairing one layer exposes the next.
stage.verifyAndTamper.ledgerIntact: Your real ledger is intact: the demonstration ran only on a copy.
stage.recallAndDebrief.instruction: A laboratory finds an unacceptable pesticide residue in the original green coffee batch. Trace forward to identify exactly the affected lots, and only those.
stage.recallAndDebrief.scopeNotice: Use the provenance recorded on the ledger, not the product name. One lot closely resembles the contaminated one: same co-operative, harvested a day later, roasted the same day at the same plant.
stage.recallAndDebrief.recallPending: Answer the scope question above first. The recall is filed for exactly the lots you selected.
stage.recallAndDebrief.accuracyExact: The recall scope is exact: every affected lot and no others.
stage.recallAndDebrief.accuracyMissed: {count} affected lot(s) missed. Contaminated product is still on the shelf.
stage.recallAndDebrief.accuracyOver: {count} unaffected lot(s) recalled. Good stock is destroyed needlessly.

validation.heading: Business rule check results
validation.someFailed: The transaction was not accepted. Review the unsatisfied rules below.
validation.actorAuthorized: The actor is authorized to submit this transaction.
validation.actorNotAuthorized: The actor is not authorized to submit transactions on this network.
validation.organizationUnknown: The submitting organization is not among the recognized organizations.
validation.actionNotPermitted: This organization is not permitted to perform the selected action.
validation.producerMismatch: The batch must be created by the same organization that is submitting the transaction.
validation.organizationInactive: The organization is no longer active on this network.
validation.assetIdUnique: The batch identifier has not been used before.
validation.assetIdAlreadyExists: This batch identifier already exists on the ledger. Each batch needs its own identifier.
validation.quantityMustBePositive: The quantity must be greater than 0.
validation.quantityNotANumber: The quantity must be a number.
validation.unitCompatible: The unit of measure is compatible.
validation.packageSizeRequired: When the unit is packages, declare the mass of each package so the system can compare masses.
validation.packageSizeNotApplicable: Only declare a package mass when the unit is packages.
validation.actorOrganizationMismatch: The actor does not belong to the organization named in the transaction.
validation.assetExists: The batch exists on the ledger.
validation.assetDoesNotExist: This batch is not on the ledger yet. It must be created before anything can be done to it.
validation.batchNotRecalled: The batch has not been recalled.
validation.batchRecalled: The batch has been recalled and can no longer be moved or processed.
validation.certificateExpired: The certificate had expired at the time it was used.
validation.certificateDateInvalid: The certificate's validity date is not usable.
validation.certifierUnknown: The issuing body is not among the organizations on this network.
validation.certifierNotRecognized: The issuing body is not recognized on this network. A hash proves a file has not changed; it does not prove the issuer had authority.
validation.certifierWrongType: This organization is not a certification body.
validation.certifierNotAuthorized: This organization is not permitted to issue certificates on the network.
validation.currentCustodianOk: The submitting organization currently holds the batch.
validation.currentCustodianRequired: Rejected: the submitting organization is not the party currently holding the batch.
validation.custodianMismatch: The sender named in the transaction is not the current custodian on the ledger.
validation.currentOwnerOk: The submitting organization is the current owner.
validation.currentOwnerRequired: Rejected: the submitting organization is not the current owner of the batch.
validation.ownerMismatch: The transferring party does not match the owner on the ledger.
validation.ownershipUnchanged: The transaction moves custody only; ownership is unchanged.
validation.ownershipMustNotTransferWithC: Rejected: handing goods to a carrier transfers custody only. The carrier holds the goods, it does not buy them, so ownership stays with the co-operative.
validation.receiverUnknown: The receiving party is not among the recognized organizations.
validation.receiverInactive: The receiving party is no longer active on this network.
validation.receiverSameAsSender: The receiving party cannot be the same as the sender.
validation.recallAuthorized: The submitting organization has recall authority.
validation.recallNotAuthorized: Only the regulator may issue a recall.
validation.validStateTransition: The batch's state permits this action.
validation.invalidStateTransition: This action cannot be performed on a batch in its current state.
validation.quantityAvailable: The received quantity matches the ledger.
validation.quantityBelowLedger: The quantity actually received is lower than the ledger records. A correction transaction is needed to explain the difference.
validation.quantityExceedsLedger: The received quantity is greater than the ledger holds.
validation.quantityNotComparable: The masses cannot be compared because unit information is missing.
validation.documentHashPresent: The document carries a valid hash.
validation.documentHashMissing: The document hash is missing. Recording only a filename means the ledger cannot detect the file being swapped.
validation.documentAnchorMissing: The document has not been anchored on chain.
validation.shipmentBeforeReceipt: The dispatch and receipt are in a valid order.
validation.receiptBeforeShipment: A batch cannot be received before it was sent.
validation.noShipmentRecorded: No dispatch has been recorded for this batch.
validation.receiptNotDuplicated: The batch has not been received before.
validation.receiptDuplicated: This batch has already been received.
validation.timestampInvalid: The transaction time is not valid.
validation.timestampBeforePrevious: The transaction time is earlier than the batch's most recent record.
validation.transformationInputMissing: The input batch for the transformation could not be found.
validation.transformationOutputUnique: The output batch identifier has not been used.
validation.transformationOutputExists: The output batch identifier already exists on the ledger.
validation.transformationOutputSameAsInp: The output batch must differ from the input batch.
validation.transformationYieldOk: The output mass is valid against the input.
validation.transformationOutputExceedsIn: The output mass exceeds the input mass. Processing cannot create mass.
validation.correctionReferenceOk: The correction references a valid transaction.
validation.correctionReferenceMissing: The transaction to be corrected could not be found.
validation.correctionReferencesRejected: A rejected transaction cannot be corrected: it never changed anything.
validation.correctionOfCorrection: A correction cannot correct another correction. Reference the original record.
validation.correctionReasonRequired: A reason is required. The original record is preserved unchanged, so the reason is the only explanation anyone reading the ledger later will have.
validation.correctionFieldRequired: The field being corrected must be named.
validation.correctionValuesIdentical: The corrected value is the same as the incorrect one.
check.certificateStorage.question: The quality certificate is a PDF of about 2 MB. How should it be recorded on the ledger?
check.certificateStorage.optionWholeFile: Store the entire PDF file on chain.
check.certificateStorage.optionHash: Store the file off chain, and record its hash and metadata on chain.
check.certificateStorage.optionFilename: Record only the filename on chain.
check.certificateStorage.feedback: Off chain with an on-chain hash is the right choice. A large file need not sit on the chain; the hash is enough to detect whether it changed. Recording only a filename lets the file behind that name be swapped without the ledger noticing.
check.certificateStorage.connection: You have just anchored the certificate's hash. The hash tells you whether the file changed; it does not tell you whether what the file says is true.
check.certificateIssuer.question: A second certificate arrives with a valid hash, issued by a consulting company that is not recognized on the network. What do you do?
check.certificateIssuer.optionAcceptHash: Accept it: a valid hash proves the document has not been altered.
check.certificateIssuer.optionReject: Reject it: the issuer has no certification authority on this network.
check.certificateIssuer.optionAcceptNote: Accept it, but note that it is unverified.
check.certificateIssuer.feedback: Reject it. A hash proves only that the document has not changed since it was anchored; it says nothing about whether the issuer had any standing. Integrity is not authority.
check.certificateIssuer.connection: RULE_CERTIFIER_AUTHORIZED rejected that transaction. On a permissioned network, the list of recognized organizations is part of the trust mechanism.
check.custodyScope.question: The co-operative hands the batch to the carrier for transport to the plant. What does this transaction transfer?
check.custodyScope.feedback: Custody only. The carrier holds and transports the batch, but does not buy it. Ownership stays with the co-operative until a separate sale takes place.
check.custodyScope.connection: Choosing both makes RULE_OWNERSHIP_UNCHANGED_ON_CUSTODY_TRANSFER reject the transaction. This is the most important distinction in the whole activity.
check.transportCondition.question: The sensor reports 72% humidity against a 70% limit. How should this be recorded?
check.transportCondition.optionIgnore: Ignore it: the difference is small.
check.transportCondition.optionInspect: Record the excursion, flag the batch for inspection, keep the raw dataset off chain and anchor its hash.
check.transportCondition.optionWholeFile: Store the whole sensor dataset on chain.
check.transportCondition.feedback: Record it and flag for inspection. An excursion does not by itself condemn a batch; it creates an obligation to look. The blockchain records the reading, a person decides what it means.
check.transportCondition.connection: Sensor data reaches the ledger through an authorized data source. A blockchain cannot measure humidity by itself.
check.transformationProvenance.question: After roasting, how is the roasted batch recorded relative to the green coffee it came from?
check.transformationProvenance.optionInd: As an entirely new batch, unrelated to the input.
check.transformationProvenance.optionLin: As a new batch with a provenance link to the input, which is marked as consumed.
check.transformationProvenance.optionDel: The input batch is deleted from the ledger.
check.transformationProvenance.feedback: The new batch keeps a link to its input, and the input is marked as consumed rather than deleted. That link is exactly what makes forward tracing from green coffee to a finished package possible.
check.transformationProvenance.connectio: Without that link, at the recall stage you would have no way to know which packages came from the contaminated batch.
check.tamperIntegrity.question: You just altered an old record on a copy of the ledger and saw that block and every block after it report an error. What does that prove?
check.tamperIntegrity.optionPrevents: Blockchain prevents anyone from altering old data.
check.tamperIntegrity.optionDetectable: Blockchain does not prevent alteration, but makes an alteration impossible to hide.
check.tamperIntegrity.optionLastBlock: Only the last block is affected.
check.tamperIntegrity.feedback: Blockchain produces evidence of tampering; it does not prevent tampering. Because each block carries the previous block's hash, altering an old record invalidates every block that follows.
check.tamperIntegrity.connection: That demonstration ran on a copy. Your real ledger was not touched.
check.dataGovernance.question: Classify each of these data items according to how it should be handled in this scenario.
check.dataGovernance.categoryOffChainHas: Store off chain and anchor the hash
check.dataGovernance.categoryDoNotCollec: Should not be collected for this purpose
check.dataGovernance.feedback: The right classification depends on the situation, not on a universal rule. Here: batch identifier and recall status are needed by everyone, so they go on chain; large files stay off chain with only a hash anchored; wholesale price is commercially sensitive; a consumer's home address is not needed for traceability at all and should not be collected.
check.recallScope.question: The laboratory found an unacceptable residue in green coffee batch BAT_GREEN_COFFEE_001. Which lots fall within the recall?
check.recallScope.optionNearMissLot: Packaged lot BAT_PACKAGED_COFFEE_002 (Arabica Lam Dong 100g, roasted the same day at the same plant)
check.recallScope.feedback: The recall covers the roasted batch and the packaged lot derived from the contaminated green coffee. BAT_PACKAGED_COFFEE_002 looks almost identical: same variety, same region, same plant, roasted the same day. But it came from a different green batch and has no provenance path to the contaminated one. Only provenance separates them.
check.recallScope.connection: Recalling too widely destroys good stock; recalling too narrowly leaves contaminated product on the shelf. Both are errors, with different consequences.
check.blockchainNecessity.question: When is blockchain more clearly warranted than a centralized database?
check.blockchainNecessity.optionAlwaysBe: Always: blockchain is more secure than a database.
check.blockchainNecessity.optionIndepend: When independent organizations need shared records but do not want one participant controlling the whole system.
check.blockchainNecessity.optionFaster: When higher throughput than a database is needed.
check.blockchainNecessity.optionGuarante: When a guarantee that the input data is true is needed.
check.blockchainNecessity.feedback: Blockchain is most defensible when independent organizations need shared records and none should control the whole system. If a single organization owns the data, a database is usually simpler, faster and cheaper. And no system can guarantee that the input data is true.
hint.certificateStorage: Consider what actually needs verifying: the file's contents, or whether the file has changed.
hint.custodyVersusOwnership: Ask: after this transaction, who may sell the batch, and who physically has it?
hint.correctionMechanism: A committed record cannot be edited directly. Look for a way to add a new record that links to the incorrect one.
hint.transformationYield: Roasting drives off moisture, so the output mass is always lower than the input mass.
hint.recallProvenance: Do not rely on product name or roasting date. Follow the provenance links from the contaminated batch.

message.inputTruth: Blockchain helps preserve and trace submitted records, but it does not automatically prove that a physical-world claim is true.
message.correction: Committed records are not edited or deleted. A new correction transaction is added and linked to the original record.
message.sharedLedger: A shared ledger does not necessarily mean that every participant can see every item of data.
message.blockchainNecessity: Blockchain is most defensible when independent organizations need shared records and do not want one participant to control the entire system.
message.physicalDigital: Reliable traceability also requires identifiers, procedures, sensors, inspections, authorized data sources, and organizational accountability.
message.tamperDetected: The hash chain is no longer consistent. Altering the old record has invalidated this block and every block after it.

stage.anchorCertificate.hashNotice: The hash is computed from the certificate content bundled with the activity. No file upload is needed.
stage.anchorCertificate.issueAction: Issue the certificate for the batch
stage.anchorCertificate.suspiciousBody: A second certificate has arrived for the same batch. Its hash is valid, but the issuer is not among the network's recognized organizations. Try submitting it and see what happens.
stage.anchorCertificate.suspiciousFeedba: The transaction was rejected. A valid hash proves only that the file has not changed; it does not prove the issuer had authority. Integrity is not authority.
stage.shipAndMonitor.custodyAction: Hand the batch to the carrier
stage.shipAndMonitor.roleSwitch: You now take the role of logistics coordinator at the carrier.
stage.shipAndMonitor.oracleNotice: Sensor data reaches the ledger through an authorized data source (an oracle). A blockchain cannot measure humidity itself.
stage.receiveAndCorrect.manifestQuantity: Quantity on the manifest already recorded on the ledger
stage.receiveAndCorrect.weighedQuantity: Quantity actually weighed at the plant
stage.receiveAndCorrect.discrepancyBody: The manifest was filed by the co-operative's shipping clerk before the batch left the warehouse, and is already on the ledger. You cannot edit or delete that record.
stage.receiveAndCorrect.purchaseAction: Record the purchase of the batch
stage.receiveAndCorrect.reasonSuggestion: Reweighing at the plant gave 100 kg, not the 1000 kg on the manifest.
stage.receiveAndCorrect.reasonHint: The original record is preserved unchanged, so this reason is the only explanation anyone reading the ledger later will have.
stage.transformBatch.yieldNotice: Roasting drives off moisture, so the output mass is always lower than the input. The system checks this by converting both sides to grams.
stage.packageAndDistribute.conversionNot: The output count of 820 packages is larger than the input figure of 82 kg. The system compares actual mass rather than raw numbers, so this transaction is valid.
stage.packageAndDistribute.mirrorNotice: In step 4, custody moved while ownership stayed. The next transaction does the reverse: ownership moves to the distributor while the goods remain at the plant.

terms.transactionDefinition: A record of a supply-chain event, submitted to the network for validation and writing into the ledger.
terms.blockDefinition: A group of transactions written together, containing the hash of the previous block.
terms.hashDefinition: A string computed from data content. If the data changes, the hash changes, so it can be used to detect alteration.
terms.ledgerDefinition: The whole chain of blocks and the transactions recorded in them.
terms.worldStateDefinition: The current state of each asset, derived from the whole transaction history.
terms.smartContractDefinition: A program running on the blockchain network that checks and enforces business rules. In this simulation, the rule engine plays that role.
terms.ownershipDefinition: The right of ownership over goods. The owner may sell the batch.
terms.custodyDefinition: Physical possession of goods. The custodian is holding them but does not necessarily own them.
terms.provenanceDefinition: The relationships between lots, showing which was derived from which.
terms.endorsementDefinition: Approval of a transaction by the organizations concerned, before it is recorded.
terms.orderingServiceDefinition: The component that puts transactions in order before they are written into a block.
terms.oracleDefinition: An authorized external data source that brings real-world information onto the ledger, such as a sensor reading.
terms.permissionedBlockchainDefinition: A blockchain network on which only recognized organizations may write transactions.
